title: The 8 Levels of Panic Cleaning
house: A bustling metropolitan neighborhood populated by anthropomorphic fruit and vegetable people, featuring cramped apartments, high-end appliance stores, and a central subway station with glowing digital billboards.
catchphrase: The number never lies, but the dirt is invisible.
links: Level 1 mentions the loud vacuum cleaner heard next door from Level 4.
Level 3 references the same broken elevator that Level 6 gets trapped in.
Level 7 buys cheap cleaning spray from the same kiosk where Level 2 works.

levels.name: Pip, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 1. Five minutes until the boiler repairman arrives, and my apartment looks like a tornado hit a landfill. I am Pip, a stressed-out little Blueberry guy drowning in laundry while my forehead glows 05 minutes. I frantically shove three weeks of dirty socks under the couch cushion before he sees them. Sweat drips down my blue rind as the clock ticks down every single second without mercy. Suddenly, a heavy knock echoes through the thin walls, vibrating right through my tired feet. You call this a living space? It is a landfill for low-level peasants. My forehead badge flickers frantically and drops down to absolute zero as panic freezes my veins. A hidden compartment in the floor suddenly pops open, revealing a glowing map that changes everything about this building. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Sunny, 25, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 2. Fifteen minutes on the clock and I am spraying window cleaner like my life depends on it. I am Sunny, an energetic Lemon woman scrubbing coffee rings off my glass table. Every streak I miss feels like a personal failure broadcast to the entire neighborhood. I grab a paper towel and wipe furiously until my citrus skin tingles with exhaustion. Your dusting is pathetic, even a spoiled orange could do better. She sneers and kicks dirt right onto my freshly mopped kitchen tiles. My cleaning score plummets instantly while hot tears sting my citrus eyes. Just as I am about to give up, the intercom blares an emergency warning about a building-wide inspection. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Brocco, 29, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 3. Thirty minutes left and I am treating my living room rug like a crime scene investigation. I am Brocco, a meticulous Broccoli man armed with a high-powered steam vacuum. I calculate every square inch of carpet to ensure zero particles remain on the floorboards. My stalks quiver as the digital timer counts down another stressful minute. Your baseboards are caked in grime, you will never pass inspection. He runs a white cotton gloved finger along my wooden mantelpiece and holds up a speck of dust. My steam vacuum short-circuits and sparks fly across the hardwood floor in total chaos. The lights in the entire building flicker off, plunging us into absolute darkness before a mysterious red siren starts spinning. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Coco, 31, Carpenter
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 4. Forty-five minutes before arrival and my apartment smells like a chemical weapon testing site. I am Coco, a tough brown Kokosnuss man scrubbing my wooden floors with industrial bleach. I scrub harder to eliminate every trace of sawdust from my latest carpentry project. My tough outer shell aches as I fight against the relentless ticking of the clock. Your harsh bleach stinks up the entire hallway, amateur hour is over. She picks up my garbage can and tosses it right out into the common corridor. My wooden floorboards buckle under the moisture and my hard shell begins to crack. A strange ticking sound starts coming from behind the wall panels, drowning out the noise of our argument. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Peach, 26, Florist
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 5. One hour and fifteen minutes left, and every cushion in this house has been fluffed into submission. I am Peach, a soft-skinned Peach woman delicately arranging lavender bouquets. I spray floral water across the room to mask the scent of panic and bleach coming from downstairs. My hands tremble as I adjust the decorative ribbons on every single vase. This room lacks atmospheric warmth, your lighting choices are frankly barbaric. He unscrews my warm lamps and replaces them with blinding medical-grade white bulbs. My delicate floral arrangements wither under the harsh glare while my cheeks burn. A shadow passes by the window outside, making me realize we are being watched by someone from the top floor. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Avoc, 28, Designer
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 6. Two hours of intense scrubbing and my minimalist apartment looks like an art gallery showroom. I am Avoc, a sleek Avocado man wiping down my stainless steel refrigerator. I polish every metal surface until it reflects my stressed expression with crystal clarity. My designer furniture is arranged with absolute geometric precision to please any inspector. Stop rearranging your furniture at this hour, some of us live in a pigsty and need sleep. He screams obscenities through the drywall while spilling coffee all over my clean welcome mat. My expensive designer rug takes a direct hit and stains instantly in front of me. Sirens start wailing outside as the front security gates automatically lock down all apartments. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Berry, 34, Curator
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 7. Three hours of meticulous organizing and my entire home is a temple of sterile perfection. I am Berry, a glossy Red Strawberry woman inspecting every single book spine on my shelf. I align each volume by height and color spectrum to create an illusion of eternal calm. My seed-studded face beams with pride as I complete the ultimate cleaning checklist. Your cleaning checklist is utterly absurd, nobody lives like this in the real world. She laughs hysterically and accidentally knocks over a bottle of blue cleaning liquid. My custom velvet sofa absorbs the chemical dye while my heart shatters into pieces. A mysterious key drops out from inside the ruined sofa cushion, unlocking a secret countdown on my forehead badge. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Krono, 40, Master Caretaker
levels.story: The 8 levels of panic cleaning. Level 8. Five hours of total mastery and I am the one who scheduled every single panic cleaning in this building. I am Krono, the majestic Dragonfruit man holding the master keys to all eight apartments. I oversee this entire ecosystem of anxiety and ensure every fruit person stays on edge. You were never cleaning for a repairman, you were cleaning to prove your worth to each other. The entire building gasps as the front door swings wide open to reveal an empty room with a golden mirror. The number on our foreheads didn't measure dirt, it measured how much we cared what others thought. Suddenly, all the digital badges shatter into dust, leaving us free from our endless obsession. What is the true number glowing on your forehead right now?
